content:
Apple updated its TestFlight app back in July, adding basic search functionality. You might think such a minor change would be universally welcomed, but the same TestFlight update also introduced a rather annoying bug for many users.

Speaking for myself, I wasn't noticeably affected by this bug. So I thought the TestFlight update was a simple but important improvement at the time.

Sometimes a small change can have a big impact. That's especially true for users with a large library of pre-loaded beta software when it comes to Apple's latest TestFlight update. Apple has just updated TestFlight for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and other platforms. The new version 4.3 adds "a search bar to quickly find apps."

Looking back, I actually noticed something odd and noted it at the end of the article (though I had it backwards in my assessment at the time):

I suspect the reason I didn't notice this bug is that I merged my separate iCloud and App Store Apple IDs two years ago, preserving several years' worth of TestFlight history. Although the process was a hassle, it was worth it for me.

Anyway, the TestFlight bug was also spotted by John Vorhees at MacStories:

So you can imagine my excitement when I saw Zac Hall at 9to5Mac write that TestFlight had added a search bar. I thought: "Finally!" I immediately stopped what I was doing to update the app. [...] However, there's a big "but" to this story. Previously, TestFlight beta items were listed in reverse chronological order, which I personally loved. [...] Now these expired betas have been jumbled in among the active TestFlight betas, arranged alphabetically, and the list of expired betas appears to have expanded to include every beta I had ever participated in. By my rough count, that's nearly 800 app entries for me. Needless to say, there are very few active betas among them. The search function helps, but scrolling through to find anything is now impossible.

Then in August, John Gruber wrote a piece on Daring Fireball about the TestFlight update and bug:

Last night, more than a month after this bug appeared (and was flagged by Vorhees), Apple finally updated TestFlight for the first time. Although the update notes only mention bug fixes, it does indeed fix the aforementioned bug.

TestFlight version 4.3.1 is a fix for users affected by the regression issue.
